title: Rectangular prism
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees, and the translation vector set to zero, zero, and zero. On the first face, draw a two-dimensional sketch consisting of a closed loop with six lines. Start by drawing the first line from the origin to the point zero point zero three three nine, zero. Continue with the second line from this point to zero point zero three three nine, zero point zero three three nine. Draw the third line from this point to zero point zero three one nine, zero point zero three three nine. The fourth line should go from this point to zero point zero three one nine, zero point zero zero two. The fifth line should extend from this point to the origin along the y-axis, and finally, close the loop with the sixth line back to the origin. Apply a scale factor of zero point zero three three nine to the entire two-dimensional sketch. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into three dimensions by rotating it using the same Euler angles and translating it using the same translation vector. Extrude the transformed two-dimensional sketch zero point seven five units along the normal direction to create a new solid body. The final dimensions of the rectangular prism are length zero point zero three three nine three six six five one five eight three seven one zero four one units, width zero point zero three three nine three six six five one five eight three seven one zero four one units, and height zero point seven five units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0339, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0339, 0.0339) \
     .lineTo(0.0319, 0.0339) \
     .lineTo(0.0319, 0.002) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.002) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# Note: CAD-Query does not directly support Euler angles, so we need to use rotation matrices
# The given Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

lanes.label: GLM-5.3 Flash (high)
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# L-shaped angle profile
leg = 0.0339      # leg length of the angle
thk = 0.011       # material thickness
length = 0.75     # extrusion length along X

# Profile drawn on the YZ plane, extruded along X
r = (
    cq.Workplane("YZ")
    .polyline([
        (0, 0),
        (leg, 0),
        (leg, thk),
        (thk, thk),
        (thk, leg),
        (0, leg),
        (0, 0),
    ])
    .close()
    .extrude(length)
)

lanes.label: Kimi K3 (high)
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

L = 0.7500
w = 0.0339
t = 0.0050

r = (
    cq.Workplane("YZ")
    .moveTo(0, 0)
    .lineTo(w, 0)
    .lineTo(w, w)
    .lineTo(w - t, w)
    .lineTo(w - t, t)
    .lineTo(0, t)
    .close()
    .extrude(L)
)
